vs.backdropSub: The backdrop belongs to marketing and auth surfaces only. The application workspace keeps a clean, decoration-free background.
vs.buttonsSub: Solid buttons lift one pixel and take a soft shadow on hover. The focus ring opens over 150ms.
vs.card1Body: Only opacity and transform animate — never width, height or position.
vs.card2Body: Every directional move is multiplied by --dir-sign and flips on its own.
vs.card3Body: With prefers-reduced-motion enabled, every decorative animation is switched off.
vs.cardsSub: Each card follows the previous one by 60ms and lifts a single pixel on hover.
vs.drawerBody: The drawer opens from the correct reading edge: the right in LTR, the left in RTL. The slide runs 400ms on transform only.
vs.drawerBody2: The same pattern powers the mobile navigation drawer and the log inspector.
vs.glowSub: A large radial at top center — always behind the content.
vs.gridSub: 44px lines at the lowest contrast, fading out toward the bottom.
vs.heroSub: Every element arrives on a schedule: eyebrow, title, description, buttons, and finally the product preview. Opacity and transform only — the layout never shifts.
vs.meshSub: Nodes and links at a gentle angle — topology, not decoration.
vs.modalBody: The modal enters with a backdrop fade and a 12px travel of the card — 250ms in total.
vs.motionSub: Fast 150ms for hover and focus, normal 250ms for buttons and menus, slow 400ms for entrances and drawers. 400ms is the system ceiling.
vs.noteReduced: Turn on “reduce motion” in your system and every entrance, backdrop and floating layer appears instantly, without movement. The behaviour is built into the motion tokens and the prefers-reduced-motion shortcut.
vs.overlaysSub: The modal fades and travels 250ms; drawers slide up to the 400ms ceiling and open from the correct edge.
vs.pageSub: Backdrop layers, motion tokens and micro-interactions — live
vs.tabBody1: The active tab indicator moves with a transform — never with width or position.
